newsitem.title: USA: United Technologies unit to settle U.S. suit.
newsitem.headline: United Technologies unit to settle U.S. suit.

text.p: Jet engine maker Pratt & Whitney, a unit of United Technologies Corp, said Wednesday it will pay $14.8 million to settle a lawsuit brought by the U.S. government.
The lawsuit accused the company of helping a former Israeli general defraud the U.S. government of millions of dollars, Pratt said in a statement.
Pratt said it acted in good faith at the direction of General Rami Dotan and was itself a victim of the fraud.

The government filed the civil suit in 1995, alleging that Pratt played a role in a conspiracy to divert $10 million in U.S. military aid into a slush fund controlled exclusively by Dotan, a retired Israeli Air force general.
Pratt's statement said it was returning to the government "funds which it has held for several years, but has never laid claim to, as well as interest on that money."
The company is also returning the profit on certain subcontracts, together with interest.
Pratt released its statement late on Tuesday, and a Pratt official told Reuters the amount of the settlement on Wednesday.
